Laura / team — I pulled together a matrix and recommended draft snippets (see attached). High level recommendations: 

1) Output ownership: Accept customer ownership of outputs in the Order Form clause, with one carveout — Redwood may use customer outputs to the extent necessary to provide the service (e.g., caching, delivery) but not for model training unless the customer opts in. Draft snippet: 
"Customer retains ownership of Outputs. Redwood may use Outputs solely to operate, maintain, and secure the Service; any use of Outputs for model training or to create new models requires explicit Customer Consent."

2) Training & feedback: Recommend a default opt-out for training on customer-submitted prompts and uploads, but a mandatory (nonexclusive, royalty-free) feedback license limited: 
- Scope: aggregated and deidentified feedback and telemetry used to improve safety, performance, and diagnostics.
- Duration: 12 months retention for telemetry used in model improvements (operationally reasonable).
- Exclusions: Customer can flag datasets or projects for exclusion.

3) Feedback license language (short form): 
"Customer grants Redwood a nonexclusive, royalty-free license to use de-identified Feedback solely to improve Redwood's services and models, subject to Customer-designated exclusions. Feedback will not be attributed to Customer and will be retained no longer than 12 months for improvement purposes."

Risks: Acero may push for longer retention or broader downstream rights. Ops consideration (Grace): any opt-in retrain path must include a documented data ingestion/segregation workflow and a clear billing/credits model.

Attached: IP_Clearance_Matrix_v1.xlsx, proposed_feedback_license_snippet.txt

Ben Carter
Legal, Redwood Inference

Quick ops read: 
- The 12-month telemetry retention is reasonable operationally, but we need a clear mechanism for per-customer exclusions (one ticket + enforcement workflow).
- For any opt-in retraining, recommend we require a signed Appendix (Order Form addendum) that specifies scope, dataset delivery method (SFTP or VPC), validation checklist, and extra billed credits.
- If Acero requires "no training unless explicit opt-in", we should be explicit about what counts as "training" vs "improvement": logging/metrics -> improvement; dataset ingestion for model retrain -> training.

Action items for Laura: propose the two-paragraph compromise to Acero (customer owns outputs; Redwood gets limited de-identified feedback license; retrain requires opt-in appendix). I'll link to an ops playbook once Ben/Mari have language.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
